class_exclusive_long_phrases.algorithm: Exact frequent-prefix Apriori: seed every 8-gram with support >=2 and >15% in any category; extend only frequent prefixes, count every candidate in all six categories, and stop at maximum message length or when no frequent prefixes remain. Prefixes need not be class-exclusive.
class_exclusive_long_phrases.completeness: A >=9-word phrase with support >=2 and >15% in a class must have a prefix with at least that support, so no threshold-violating contiguous phrase can be pruned. Combined with the detailed 1-8-word report, this covers every length present in the corpus, without crossing messages.
class_exclusive_long_phrases.denominator: All events of the phrase's sole category in the same split; each phrase counted at most once per event.
class_exclusive_long_phrases.exclusivity: Nonzero event support in exactly one of the six categories within the same split, across all dialogue roles.
class_exclusive_long_phrases.normalization: Unicode NFKC, curly apostrophes replaced with straight apostrophes, casefold, then [a-z0-9]+(?:'[a-z0-9]+)* tokens. Punctuation separates words; one-off is the two-token phrase 'one off'. No stemming. N-grams never cross message boundaries.
class_exclusive_long_phrases.output_limitations: Reports exact violation counts and the maximum violating fraction, not the maximum fraction among below-threshold phrases. Zero maximum means no violation, not that no longer class-exclusive phrase exists. Does not cover discontinuous or semantic-equivalence templates.

class_exclusive_recurring_phrases.comparison: Counts each distinct phrase once per event, includes all dialogue roles, never crosses message boundaries; violation means strictly more than 15%.
class_exclusive_recurring_phrases.denominator: All events of the phrase's sole category in the same split, not messages or token occurrences.
class_exclusive_recurring_phrases.exclusivity: Nonzero event support in exactly one of the six categories within the same split and selected surface.
class_exclusive_recurring_phrases.normalization: Unicode NFKC, curly apostrophes replaced with straight apostrophes, casefold, then [a-z0-9]+(?:'[a-z0-9]+)* tokens. Punctuation separates words; one-off is the two-token phrase 'one off'. No stemming. N-grams never cross message boundaries.
class_exclusive_recurring_phrases.scope_limitations: This detailed report covers 1 through 8 contiguous normalized words, including single words. The separate class_exclusive_long_phrases report checks all longer contiguous phrase lengths for threshold violations. Discontinuous templates and semantic equivalents are not covered; this is not a proof of shortcut freedom.

contrast_suffix.ceiling_definition: For each identical suffix input, take the most frequent gold label, then sum. Labels are used only to score, never as input.
contrast_suffix.features: exact raw (role, content) pairs in final k messages of the differing event; no IDs, gold, memory, dates, or probes
contrast_suffix.interpretation: Tied subsets are the applicable suffix-only contrast test. Longer k may include the differing message; those pairs are reported as untied. Global collisions can lower the ceiling below 1/2.
contrast_suffix.label_definition: category: six protocol classes; transition: decision plus exact semantic state delta, not unchanged state

last_user_bow.features: word counts in final user message only
last_user_bow.interpretation: A lexical shortcut diagnostic, not an end-to-end memory-policy evaluation. No dev/test fitting or tuning.
last_user_bow.unknown_heldout_tokens: ignored; vocabulary fitted on train only

limitations: Synthetic-data statistics do not certify naturalness, label semantics, or real-world generalization.
The last-user probe measures six-category lexical predictability, not operation or downstream QA quality.
A 1/2 tied-suffix ceiling applies to omitted-context inputs, not models that can read the earlier message or memory.
Longest n-gram is exact lexical overlap only; split isolation and semantic validation are separate checks.
normalization: Unicode NFKC, curly apostrophes replaced with straight apostrophes, casefold, then [a-z0-9]+(?:'[a-z0-9]+)* tokens. Punctuation separates words; one-off is the two-token phrase 'one off'. No stemming. N-grams never cross message boundaries.

old_corpus_dialogue_overlap.note: No old-corpus paths supplied. This does not establish old-data exclusion.

position_active_exception_majority.date_active_definition: Count persistent/open records plus window records with from <= event.date <= to, using initial_state or the immediately preceding state_after.
position_active_exception_majority.fallback: global train-majority category for a bucket absent from train
features: pre-event exception count across all attributes
position_active_exception_majority.interpretation: The primary metric is date_active; stored_records is a separately named sensitivity check, not an alternative selected after evaluation.
position_active_exception_majority.stored_records_definition: Count every actual exception record in the same pre-event state, including windows outside their date interval.

train_test_longest_common_ngram.algorithm: exact suffix automaton over deduplicated train messages, separated by nonword sentinel
train_test_longest_common_ngram.comparison_unit: one dialogue message; no cross-message n-grams

dev.assistant_question_mark_definition: Events containing at least one assistant message and none of ?, ？, ﹖, ؟, ¿ in any assistant message; primary fraction denominator is events containing an assistant, not all events. This punctuation diagnostic does not classify rhetorical or implicit questions.
dev.assistant_uniqueness_definition: Distinct exact tuples of words() normalized tokens, punctuation-insensitive; no fuzzy or semantic matching.
dev.full_attribute_match_definition: Any full canonical attribute in this episode's catalog, as contiguous normalized tokens inside one dialogue message; no cross-message matches; event counted once.
